The stream-track figure (gS1) is built and in the repo, but left out on your call — its gradient is correct and finite-difference-validated here, while an unexplained ~20% discrepancy still appears on some py3.14 CI runs. The three orbit-integration figures (g8, g12, g15) are included but carry June numbers: their measurements are cross-environment and cannot be rebuilt by a plain harness run, so they were not re-measured tonight.

New & re-measured

gF1 — FR by autodiff vs the exact analytic force

NEW

Every galpy potential ships a hand-coded Rforce. These six get FR as −∂Φ/∂R by autodiff instead — a basis expansion (SCF), a disc expansion (DiskSCF), a spiral pattern, a rotating bar, and composites — and land on the analytic answer.

|AD − exact| / |exact|
240 points, median residual2.45×10−16
worst case (SpiralArms)4.0×10−15
float64 ε2.22×10−16

paper/figures/gF1_autodiff_forces/gF1_autodiff_forces.pdf · click the figure to save the PNG

gD2 — autodiff through a Monte-Carlo sample of a DF

NEW

dσr/dr two independent ways: jax.grad through a 4×106-particle sample of isotropicHernquistdf, and jax.grad through the jeans.sigmar quadrature. r enters the estimator through the kernel weights, so the gradient flows without needing a differentiable draw. Error bars are the MC noise from 8 independent sub-samples. Building this figure is what surfaced galpy#1343: at the shipped inverse-CDF velocity grid the sampled σr is ~0.7% low at every radius — pre-existing, reproduced bit-identically on main.

sample vs quadrature, in units of the MC noise
derivative agreement0.6σ median
value vs 3 theory legs<0.2%
innermost point (r=4H)bias-limited, 5.5σ

paper/figures/gD2_df_sample_autodiff/gD2_df_sample_autodiff.pdf · click the figure to save the PNG

Orbit integration speed — including galax

These three are cross-environment figures: their measurements come from separate environments (galax needs its own uv venv with a matched CUDA-12 plugin), so a plain harness run cannot rebuild them. The numbers below are from June and are not re-measured on today’s code — unlike g2/g5/g6/g17 above.
